entries.title: Quenched directional escape harmonic function
entries.statement: Let E={+/-e_i:1<=i<=d}. The environment omega has probability rows omega(x,e), e in E, on Z^d, is sampled once, and the quenched walk has X_0=0 and transition P_omega(X_{n+1}=x+e|X_n=x)=omega(x,e). For fixed nonzero l in R^d put A_l={lim_n X_n dot l=+infinity}, q_l(omega)=P_omega^0(A_l), theta_x omega(y,e)=omega(x+y,e), and Kg(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)g(theta_e omega).

entries.title: Opposite-escape exclusion reduction
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF OR SOURCE-BACKED DEDUCTION; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let E={+/-e_i:1<=i<=d}. The environment omega has probability rows omega(x,e), e in E, on Z^d, is sampled once, and the quenched walk has X_0=0 and transition P_omega(X_{n+1}=x+e|X_n=x)=omega(x,e). For fixed nonzero l in R^d put A_l={lim_n X_n dot l=+infinity}, q_l(omega)=P_omega^0(A_l), theta_x omega(y,e)=omega(x+y,e), and Kg(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)g(theta_e omega). If the annealed union law P_0(A_l union A_-l) belongs to {0,1}, then the directional law P_0(A_l) in {0,1} is equivalent to excluding simultaneous positivity of P_0(A_l) and P_0(A_-l). Event disjointness by itself does not establish this exclusion.
entries.proof_text:
Proved reduction L1: exclude coexistence of opposite escapes

For deterministic nonzero l, A_l and A_-l are disjoint. The iid elliptic union zero-one theorem gives P_0(A_l union A_-l) in {0,1}. Consequently the individual zero-one target is equivalent to ruling out P_0(A_l)>0 and P_0(A_-l)>0 simultaneously: if P_0(A_l)>0 the union has probability one, and absence of negative escape makes P_0(A_l)=1. Conversely a binary positive P_0(A_l) equals one and excludes negative escape. The disjointness statement itself is elementary and does not solve the coexistence problem.
assumptions: iid strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor environment on Z^d

entries.title: Stationary-law conditional directional zero-one proof
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF OR SOURCE-BACKED DEDUCTION; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let E={+/-e_i:1<=i<=d}. The environment omega has probability rows omega(x,e), e in E, on Z^d, is sampled once, and the quenched walk has X_0=0 and transition P_omega(X_{n+1}=x+e|X_n=x)=omega(x,e). For fixed nonzero l in R^d put A_l={lim_n X_n dot l=+infinity}, q_l(omega)=P_omega^0(A_l), theta_x omega(y,e)=omega(x+y,e), and Kg(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)g(theta_e omega). Suppose the environment law P is shift-ergodic and strictly elliptic, and there is a K-invariant probability Q equivalent to P. Then the annealed probability P_0(A_l) is zero or one.
entries.proof_text:
Proved conditional lemma L2: an equivalent stationary environment law suffices

Let theta_x shift an environment by x and let Kf(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e) f(theta_e omega). Assume the environment law P is shift ergodic, is supported on strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor environments, and there exists a K-invariant probability Q equivalent to P. For a fixed l define q(omega)=P_omega^0(A_l). The Markov property and invariance of A_l under removing a finite path prefix give Kq=q.

Since 0<=q<=1, Q-invariance gives

 integral sum_e omega(0,e)[q(theta_e omega)-q(omega)]^2 dQ
 = integral [K(q^2)-q^2] dQ = 0.

Every summand is nonnegative, and every omega(0,e) is positive Q-almost surely. Thus q(theta_e omega)=q(omega) for every neighbor e, Q-almost surely and, by equivalence, P-almost surely. Countably many translations propagate this equality to all lattice shifts. Shift ergodicity implies q=c P-almost surely for some constant c. For P-almost every omega this holds at every translate visited by the walk.

For fixed such omega and the path filtration F_n, the quenched Markov property gives E_omega[1_{A_l}|F_n]=q(theta_{X_n}omega)=c. The increasing F_n generate the full path sigma-field, so conditional-expectation convergence gives c=1_{A_l} almost surely. Hence c is 0 or 1 and P_0(A_l)=c.

This argument uses stationarity only under Q; it does not assume that P itself is invariant for the environment seen from the particle.
assumptions: K-invariant probability Q equivalent to P

entries.title: Equivalence of an absolutely continuous stationary environment law
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF OR SOURCE-BACKED DEDUCTION; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let E={+/-e_i:1<=i<=d}. The environment omega has probability rows omega(x,e), e in E, on Z^d, is sampled once, and the quenched walk has X_0=0 and transition P_omega(X_{n+1}=x+e|X_n=x)=omega(x,e). Suppose P is shift-invariant, shift-ergodic, and strictly elliptic. Let theta_x omega(y,e)=omega(x+y,e) and Kg=sum_e omega(0,e)g(theta_e omega). Every K-invariant probability Q absolutely continuous with respect to P is equivalent to P.
entries.proof_text:
Proved lemma L3: absolute continuity gives equivalence here

Assume P is shift invariant and ergodic and strictly elliptic, and Q=fP is a K-invariant probability with f>=0 and integral f dP=1. A change of variables gives the adjoint formula

 K* f(omega) = sum_e omega(-e,e) f(theta_-e omega).

Invariance implies f=K*f P-almost surely. On Z={f=0}, positivity of every incoming transition implies f(theta_-e omega)=0 for every e. Thus Z is contained, modulo null sets, in every neighboring translate of Z. Those sets have the same P-measure by shift invariance, so the inclusions are equalities modulo null sets. Ergodicity gives P(Z)=0 or 1. Integral f=1 excludes P(Z)=1. Therefore f>0 P-almost surely and Q is equivalent to P. Null exceptional sets can be removed at all countably many translates. Combining with L2 gives the directional zero-one law under absolute continuity alone.
assumptions: Q is a K-invariant probability and Q is absolutely continuous with respect to P

entries.title: Incoming-mass uniform-integrability criterion
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF OR SOURCE-BACKED DEDUCTION; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let E={+/-e_i:1<=i<=d}. The environment omega has probability rows omega(x,e), e in E, on Z^d, is sampled once, and the quenched walk has X_0=0 and transition P_omega(X_{n+1}=x+e|X_n=x)=omega(x,e). Suppose P is shift-invariant, shift-ergodic, and strictly elliptic. Define f_n(omega)=sum_{x in Z^d}P_omega^x(X_n=0) and H_N=(1/N)sum_{n=0}^{N-1}f_n. If the family H_N is uniformly integrable in L1(P), then there is an absolutely continuous stationary probability for the environment viewed from the particle, and P_0(lim_n X_n dot l=+infinity) is zero or one for every fixed nonzero l in R^d.
entries.proof_text:
Proved lemma L4: a precise sufficient incoming-mass condition

For n>=0 put f_n(omega)=sum_x P_omega^x(X_n=0), where only |x|_1<=n can contribute. The law of theta_{X_n}omega under the original annealed law is f_n P: for bounded g, change variables eta=theta_x omega in sum_x integral P_omega^0(X_n=x)g(theta_x omega)dP. The resulting transition probability is P_eta^-x(X_n=0). Thus f_0=1, f_n>=0, integral f_n=1, and f_{n+1}=K*f_n.

Put H_N=(1/N)sum_{n=0}^{N-1} f_n. If the family H_N is uniformly integrable in L1(P), the Dunford-Pettis compactness theorem gives a weakly L1-convergent subsequence with limit f>=0 and integral f=1. Further,

 ||K*H_N-H_N||_1 = ||(f_N-1)/N||_1 <= 2/N.

For every bounded measurable g, weak L1 convergence applies to both g and Kg. The displayed bound implies integral f Kg=integral f g. Hence fP is K-invariant. L3 and L2 give the directional zero-one law. This is a sufficient criterion, not a consequence yet of iid ellipticity.
assumptions: uniform integrability of the stated Cesaro densities H_N

entries.title: Exact directional harmonic-energy mass balance
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF OR SOURCE-BACKED DEDUCTION; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let E={+/-e_i:1<=i<=d}. The environment omega has probability rows omega(x,e), e in E, on Z^d, is sampled once, and the quenched walk has X_0=0 and transition P_omega(X_{n+1}=x+e|X_n=x)=omega(x,e). For fixed nonzero l in R^d put A_l={lim_n X_n dot l=+infinity}, q_l(omega)=P_omega^0(A_l), theta_x omega(y,e)=omega(x+y,e), and Kg(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)g(theta_e omega). Suppose P is shift-invariant. Put f_n(omega)=sum_x P_omega^x(X_n=0), H_N=(1/N)sum_{n<N}f_n, and D_l(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)[q_l(theta_e omega)-q_l(omega)]^2. Then sum_{n>=0} integral f_n D_l dP = integral q_l(1-q_l)dP, and integral H_N D_l dP <= 1/(4N) for every N>=1. This does not assert that integral D_l dP is zero.
entries.proof_text:
Proved lemma L5: exact energy balance without a stationary law

Keep the original P, without assuming K-invariance or uniform integrability. For q(omega)=P_omega^0(A_l), define

 D_l(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)[q(theta_e omega)-q(omega)]^2 = K(q^2)(omega)-q(omega)^2.

The equality follows from Kq=q. D_l is measurable, nonnegative, and bounded by 1. The quenched conditional-expectation martingale q(theta_{X_n}omega) converges almost surely to 1_{A_l}; bounded convergence gives integral f_N q^2 -> p, where p=P_0(A_l)=integral q dP.

Adjointness gives for every n

 integral f_n D_l dP = integral f_{n+1}q^2 dP-integral f_n q^2 dP.

Telescoping and then monotone convergence yield the exact identity

 sum_{n=0}^infinity integral f_n D_l dP = p-integral q^2 dP = integral q(1-q)dP.

In particular, integral H_N D_l dP <= integral q(1-q)dP/N <= 1/(4N). This is an exact analytic bound, not an experimental rate. It is valid for strict and uniform ellipticity and does not multiply any conditional probabilities.
assumptions: q_l is the actual quenched directional escape probability

entries.title: Directional zero-one flux-covariance equivalence
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF OR SOURCE-BACKED DEDUCTION; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let E={+/-e_i:1<=i<=d}. The environment omega has probability rows omega(x,e), e in E, on Z^d, is sampled once, and the quenched walk has X_0=0 and transition P_omega(X_{n+1}=x+e|X_n=x)=omega(x,e). For fixed nonzero l in R^d put A_l={lim_n X_n dot l=+infinity}, q_l(omega)=P_omega^0(A_l), theta_x omega(y,e)=omega(x+y,e), and Kg(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)g(theta_e omega). Suppose P has iid strictly elliptic rows. Set s(omega)=sum_e omega(-e,e) and D_l(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)[q_l(theta_e omega)-q_l(omega)]^2. Then Cov_P(s,q_l^2)=integral D_l dP>=0, and P_0(A_l) in {0,1} is equivalent to Cov_P(s,q_l^2)=0.
entries.proof_text:
Proved lemma L6: full target reduced to one flux covariance

Let s(omega)=sum_e omega(-e,e)=K*1(omega). Shift invariance gives integral s dP=1, and 0<=s<=2d. The exact identity is

 integral D_l dP = integral (s-1)q^2 dP = Cov_P(s,q^2) >=0.

If this covariance is zero, D_l=0 P-almost surely. Strict positivity then gives q(theta_e omega)=q(omega) at every neighbor almost surely; shift ergodicity and the martingale argument in L2 imply p in {0,1}. Conversely, if p is zero or one, the bounded variable q with mean p is that same constant P-almost surely, so the covariance and energy vanish. Hence the fixed-direction target is equivalent to this covariance vanishing.
assumptions: iid strictly elliptic rows on Z^d
q_l is the actual quenched escape probability

entries.title: Dirichlet trap obstruction to the stationary-probability route
entries.statement: AUTHOR PROOF OR SOURCE-BACKED DEDUCTION; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. For d=3, take iid Dirichlet rows with positive parameters (1/10,1/50,1/50,1/50,1/50,1/50) ordered (+e1,+e2,+e3,-e1,-e2,-e3). These rows are strictly elliptic but are not uniformly elliptic. Their trap exponent 2 sum_i alpha_i-max_{i<=3}(alpha_i+alpha_{i+3}) is 7/25. Sabot, arXiv:1007.2565v3, Theorem 1(ii), therefore rules out an absolutely continuous invariant probability for the environment viewed from the particle. Consequently the family H_N=(1/N)sum_{n<N}sum_x P_omega^x(X_n=0) is not uniformly integrable in L1(P). This refutes that blanket proof input, not the directional zero-one law.
entries.proof_text:
Source-backed counterexample C1: the general sufficient input is false

Take d=3 and iid Dirichlet rows with parameters alpha=(1/10,1/50,1/50,1/50,1/50,1/50), ordered (+e1,+e2,+e3,-e1,-e2,-e3). Every parameter is positive, so every row is strictly positive almost surely. Countably many sites preserve almost-sure strict ellipticity. These laws are not uniformly elliptic.

Here sum alpha=1/5; the largest opposite-pair sum is 3/25; and Sabot's trap exponent is

 kappa_D=2 sum alpha-max_i(alpha_i+alpha_{i+3})=7/25<=1.

Sabot, arXiv:1007.2565v3, Theorem 1(ii), printed page 4 (PDF page index 3), states that at kappa_D<=1 there is no absolutely continuous invariant probability for the environment viewed from the particle. Its generator is K-I, so this is exactly nonexistence for K. Therefore such an invariant probability cannot be inferred from the full C0044 assumptions. By L4, H_N is not uniformly integrable for this example. This counterexample refutes the proposed blanket invariant-probability/UI input, not C0044. The nonzero mean drift (2/5)e1 is only parameter arithmetic here; no transience claim is inferred from mean drift.

The uniformly elliptic subtarget is not refuted by this nonuniform example. We have no derivation of the required invariant probability for that subtarget either.
assumptions: iid Dirichlet environment with exactly these six positive parameters

entries.title: Unproved directional flux-covariance input
entries.statement: UNPROVED INPUT IN THIS PACKET; current openness UNKNOWN because a recent primary manuscript claims a proof that this packet has not adjudicated. Let E={+/-e_i:1<=i<=d}. The environment omega has probability rows omega(x,e), e in E, on Z^d, is sampled once, and the quenched walk has X_0=0 and transition P_omega(X_{n+1}=x+e|X_n=x)=omega(x,e). For fixed nonzero l in R^d put A_l={lim_n X_n dot l=+infinity}, q_l(omega)=P_omega^0(A_l), theta_x omega(y,e)=omega(x+y,e), and Kg(omega)=sum_e omega(0,e)g(theta_e omega). For iid strictly elliptic rows, d>=3, the remaining proposed input is Cov_P(sum_e omega(-e,e),q_l^2)=0. This is equivalent to the fixed-direction zero-one target by the proved covariance reduction. Independence of the rows does not make q_l independent of the incoming rows, because q_l depends on the whole environment.

relations.rationale: The conditional proof applies stationarity to the actual quenched escape harmonic function q_l.
Both use the shift convention theta_x omega(y,e)=omega(x+y,e) and environment kernel K.
After constructing an invariant law, the stationary-law conditional proof gives the directional zero-one conclusion.
The constructed law is absolutely continuous; the support argument proves its equivalence to P.
Kq_l=q_l and the quenched escape-indicator martingale produce the energy identity.
The harmonic-energy formula D_l=K(q_l^2)-q_l^2 becomes Cov_P(K*1,q_l^2).
Nonexistence of an absolutely continuous invariant probability, by contraposition of the sufficient criterion, implies failure of uniform integrability. The counterexample does not refute L4.
The unproved covariance input is precisely equivalent to the fixed-direction target.
Both identify the remaining one-sign directional question without claiming to solve it.

Existing card asks whether P_0(A_l) belongs to {0,1}; this draft asks whether Cov_P(sum_e omega(-e,e),q_l^2)=0. L6 proves equivalence. The 2026-09-07 open label is historical and current openness remains UNKNOWN.
